rule: A head's construction is the same from every view; only the viewing angle changes - features must not change shape between views beyond what the turn causes.
Set the eyes behind the brow ridges so they sit inside the eye sockets instead of looking pasted flat on the surface.
A happy face needs wide eyes and raised brows; a smile with lowered angry brows reads as an evil grin.
Simplified, eye-pleasing highlight and shadow shapes guide the eye better than photo-accurate shading.
